messages:
Lina: heads-up I opened a PR to add an arm64 native-extension fallback for the ruby-sdk and a tiny sampleapp change for M1 devs
Carlos: link?
Lina: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/201 - summary: detect darwin/arm64 and use the prebuilt extension tarball if present; otherwise compile with extconf.rb. adds docs for local dev on M1
Maya: saw the PR, nice. CI failure in the first run was interesting: macOS-arm64 runner failed during link with 'ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64' when building ext/fasttoken
CI-Bot: build #789 failed on macos-arm64-latest — error: ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
Sami: likely we were building against x86_64-only prebuilt libs in our container image. For ext we need to ensure toolchain and arch flags are set (ARCHFLAGS="-arch arm64")
Lina: good point. I added a tiny wrapper in the ext build step: if RUBY_PLATFORM =~ /arm64|aarch64/ then set ARCHFLAGS and pass host flags to ./configure
Carlos: can you add a smoke matrix entry that runs bundler install && rake build on macos-arm64 so we don't regress? Also add a note in the README about using rbenv/ruby-build 3.x on M1
Lina: added GH actions job 'macos-arm64-smoke' — it's minimal (install deps, bundle, rake build). also added README snippet under "Local dev (Apple Silicon)"
Maya: one UX nit: instead of auto-downloading prebuilt tarballs by default, can we prefer compiling locally when dev explicitly sets ENV['REDWOOD_PREFER_LOCAL_EXT']=1 ? Less surprising for contributors
Lina: done — default still prefers prebuilt for CI speed but README documents the ENV override
Sami: for parity with python client: python wheels are published per-arch. We should document how we publish prebuilt gems (rubygems supports platform-specific gems). Are we going to push platform gems or keep tarballs on S3 and download at install?
Lina: proposal in PR: keep current rubygems publish for x86_64 and publish arm64 gems later; interim approach is S3 tarball downloads during gem install fallback. I'll open a follow-up issue for rubygems publishing automation
Carlos: can you include a minimal sampleapp Dockerfile change for local emulation? Some folks use docker buildx for arm64 testing, add a comment linking to docker buildx docs
Lina: added a one-liner in sampleapp/README: `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 -t redwood-sample .` and a note that the gem fallback won't run in Linux containers (native ext is macOS-specific)
Maya: tests: did you add a unit that stubs the downloader so we don't hit network in CI?
Lina: yes test/ext_fetcher_spec.rb stubs S3 fetch and validates the fallback path and the ENV override path. keeps it hermetic
CI-Bot: build #790 queued
Carlos: once CI is green and you file the publishing follow-up, lgtm from me
Maya: +1 from me for the documentation and test coverage
Sami: extra: add a short changelog entry under Unreleased noting arm64 dev support and the ENV toggle
Lina: added changelog line, thanks. I'll squash and merge after CI passes
